outline.chapter_title: 1. Introduction to Attention and Long‑Context Challenges
outline.description: Provides the motivation for speeding up attention, explains why attention is the computational bottleneck in Transformers, and surveys the landscape of recent research on long‑context modeling and efficient attention.
subtopics: Evolution of Transformer attention from 2017 to 2026
Quadratic time and memory cost of self‑attention
Applications that drive the need for longer contexts
Overview of existing efficiency strategies: approximation, software optimization, alternative architectures
Positioning FlashAttention‑3 within this research ecosystem

outline.description: Covers the mathematical formulation of single‑head and multi‑head attention, forward and backward passes, scaling conventions, and practical considerations such as numerical stability.
subtopics: Definition of Q, K, V matrices and dimensionalities
Scaled dot‑product attention: S, P, O computation
Row‑wise softmax with max‑stabilization
Gradient derivations for dQ, dK, dV using chain rule
Parallelism across heads, batches, sequences
Common pitfalls: underflow/overflow, precision losses

outline.description: Explains the memory hierarchy, thread hierarchy, and new hardware features relevant to FlashAttention‑3: Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA), Warp‑Group Matrix Multiply Accumulator (WGMMA), asynchronous execution model, register allocation mechanisms, and low‑precision formats.
subtopics: HBM (GMEM), L2 cache, SMEM (shared mem), RMEM (registers)
Thread hierarchies: threads → warps → warpgroups → CTA → cluster → grid
Asynchronous data movement via TMA and compliant TMA loads
Warp‑specialization: producer vs consumer warps, setmaxnreg calls
Tensor Core capabilities in Hopper: FP8 WGMMA vs FP16/BF16 WGMMA
Layout constraints for k‑major/ mn‑major operands in FP8 WGMMA

outline.chapter_title: "Standard" Attention versus FlashAttention: The Baseline Approach
outline.description: "Standard" attention implementation on GPUs versus the key innovation of FlashAttention – fusing both matmul and softmax into a single kernel to eliminate expensive global memory traffic.
subtopics: Conventional attention pipeline with intermediate reads/writes to HBM
"FlashAttention" tiling strategy and local softmax reduction
Theoretical justification that fused kernel yields exact same result as separate ops

outline.description: "FlashAttention-2" restructured algorithm that parallelizes over sequence length dimension via key/value blocks for better occupancy. Discuss its limitations on new hardware.
subtopics: _Forward_ pass in FlashAttention-2 with block strategy_
_Backward_ pass considerations_
_Occupancy vs. utilization: comparison with HX GEMM kernels_
_Identifying performance gaps on Hopper (35% vs 80–90%)_
